about: The three requests a person can make after an overpayment notice, and the official form for each.

rows.name: Appeal
rows.when: You think you were not overpaid, or the amount is wrong.
rows.time_limit: 60 days from the date you received the notice. A later appeal needs a good reason.

rows.name: Waiver
rows.official_name: Request for Waiver of Overpayment Recovery
rows.when: The overpayment was not your fault, and paying it back would cause hardship or be unfair for another reason.
rows.time_limit: No time limit. Asking within 30 days of the notice also holds off collection while Social Security decides.
rows.phone_note: When you ask for a waiver today, if the original overpayment is $2,000 or less and you believe it was not your fault, call Social Security or your local office. They may be able to process the waiver by phone.

rows.name: Lower repayment rate
rows.official_name: Request for Change in Overpayment Recovery Rate
rows.when: You agree you owe the money, but the amount being taken each month leaves you unable to meet necessary living expenses.
